Partner with the Casino Creative Studio to translate those requirements into effective creative, with the Studio retaining ownership of creative direction and execution.</li> <li>Advise Brand and agency partners on hooks, edits, cutdowns, aspect ratios and platform-native versions, so big campaign moments carry through to always-on performance and lifecycle.</li> <li>Source player insight, competitor ad libraries, creator content and platform trends to identify new angles and white space.</li> <li>Lead performance strategy/creative insight sessions and contribute a strong POV to creative brainstorms, working closely with the Casino Creative Studio.</li> <li>Present performance learnings and recommendations in GTM forums and monthly reviews, turning results into a clear story for senior leadership.</li> <li>Lead, mentor and develop an Associate, building their craft in briefing, analysis and testing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>How This Role Connects Across the Team:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partners with the internal producer, who owns production timelines and delivery, to keep briefs, priorities and the content calendar aligned.</li> <li>Partners with the Casino Creative Studio and Integrated Marketing to shape high-quality output, providing direction and feedback while respecting executional ownership.</li> <li>Partners with Brand and Integrated Marketing to embed performance best practice into campaigns, ensuring work is both distinctive and built to perform across the funnel.</li> <li>Partners with Media, Analytics and CRM to define success measures, read results and feed learnings back into strategy.</li> <li>Works with Legal, Compliance and Creative Operations to keep all creative compliant and aligned with Responsible Gaming standards.</li> <li>Partner with the affiliates teams to produce UGC briefs aligned to channel best practice, adapting content that’s optimised for performance (via creative briefs)</li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills &amp; Qualifications:</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of experience in creative strategy, performance creative or brand strategy, including 3+ years leading creative strategy for a fast-growing D2C brand, mobile app, gaming or casino business.</li> <li>Portfolio demonstrating hook-led, insight-driven creative and the performance results behind it.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of platform-native creative across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snap and app networks, including UGC and creator formats.</li> <li>Proven track record building and running creative testing programs at volume.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills, with the ability to read performance data, size results and translate them into clear recommendations.</li> <li>Excellent storytelling and writing skills, from a 6-second hook to a campaign narrative to an executive readout.</li> <li>Experience influencing brand and integrated campaigns across matrixed teams without direct ownership.</li> <li>Experience managing and developing direct reports.</li> <li>Willingness to travel occasionally for team meetings and Fanatics events.</li> </ul> <p>Depending on the role, your interview and onboarding experience may include in-person components, such as onsite interviews or Launching into Better: LIVE—a multi-day cultural immersion in New York City for full-time, non-seasonal hires. These sessions are designed to build connection and bring our culture to life, though specific travel and participation requirements will be confirmed based on your role and location. Your recruiter will provide clear guidance at each stage of the process.</p> <p>For information about our benefits, please visit&nbsp;<a href="https://benefitsatfanatics.com/">https://benefitsatfanatics.com/</a></p> <p>#li-JM3</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p></p> <p>By submitting your application, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge you have read our <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/5ff494b9931735466ce28d5b/t/69de53bde2c02c25e9c38758/1776178110037/Candidate+Privacy+Policy+April+2026.pdf" target="_blank">Candidate Privacy Policy.</a></p> <p><em>Fanatics will never ask candidates for money, banking information, or other sensitive personal information as part of the interview process. title: Product Manager
description: About us At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels. Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet. We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel. Introducing the Trainline Core Experience Team 👋 The Core Experience team looks after how our customers find and book rail travel across the UK and Europe. Our work covers search, supply from carriers and the booking experience, all in service of our purpose of empowering greener travel choices and connecting people and places. We are a collaborative group who enjoy learning from our customers and from each other. This is a brand new role, created to own what happens once a customer has found the right journey and moves towards booking: reservation details, optional extras and payment. Because it sits so close to the point of purchase, it offers a direct line to customer experience and revenue, and plenty of room to grow. You will work alongside our Search team and the Supply and Payments platform teams, with colleagues in commercial, design, data and engineering, to make booking simple and reliable for customers in every market we serve. In this role as the Product Manager, Booking Conversion, you will...🚄 Own the customer experience from the moment someone chooses a journey to a confirmed booking, setting clear goals for conversion (the share of customers who complete their booking) and revenue while enabling other teams with a stake in the journey. Run quick cycles of experimentation by forming hypotheses, testing ideas, learning from the results and iterating, while shaping a longer-term vision and roadmap for the booking journey. Use customer insight and data to understand where people hesitate or leave, and decide where to invest limited team capacity across each step of the journey. Build a deep understanding of how rail works in different markets and with different carriers. Decide when a market or carrier specific improvement is the right investment, and when to bring ideas and learnings together across markets so that value grows for customers everywhere, rather than staying in one place. Balance wider business goals from other teams, such as adding new supply, increasing booking features for each carrier, and introducing optional extras and new revenue streams, against keeping the journey simple and low in friction for customers. Partner closely with the Supply, Search, New Business, and Payments platform teams, alongside design, data and engineering, to align priorities and deliver improvements together. Communicate openly with a wide range of stakeholders, including commercial colleagues, explaining the reasoning behind decisions and sharing progress and results in a way that builds trust. Bring AI tools into your everyday work, such as prototyping, analysis and delivery, and help the team grow in confidence using them. We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍 Experience improving conversion in a digital booking, checkout or purchase journey, using data to spot opportunities and measure the impact of your changes. Hands-on experience designing and running experiments, and turning what you learn into the next set of improvements. A customer-first mindset, with the ability to combine customer insight and data to make confident decisions even when information is incomplete. Confidence setting direction for a product area, balancing near-term improvements with a longer-term vision. Clear, thoughtful communication, with the ability to explain complex trade-offs and build alignment between teams who may have different priorities. Comfort weighing limited capacity against competing demands, and explaining what you will focus on and why. Ideally, experience balancing local needs with a wider shared strategy, for example across several markets or with third-party suppliers. It is also helpful if you are familiar with travel, ticketing or payments. You may also be curious about AI tools and keen to use them to prototype ideas, analyse results and speed up delivery. More information: Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy. Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated. Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn , Instagram and Glassdoor ! title: Member of Technical Staff, Simulated Universes
description: Our mission is to make first contact with superintelligence. We are creating a superlearner that discovers all knowledge from its own experience, from elementary motor skills through to profound intellectual breakthroughs. This superlearning capability - the ability to endlessly discover knowledge and skills, without relying on human data - will be driven by the world’s most powerful reinforcement learning algorithms. The superlearner is expected to rediscover and then transcend the greatest inventions in human history, such as language, science, mathematics and technology. If successful, this will represent a scientific breakthrough of comparable magnitude to Darwin: where his law explained all life, our law will explain and build all intelligence. Role brief Intelligence cannot emerge in a void. It needs a place to grow and flourish. As a Simulated Universes Engineer, you’ll help us craft, shape and maintain the worlds in which superlearners can emerge and thrive. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons&nbsp;don’t&nbsp;feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">In 2024,&nbsp;PsiQuantum&nbsp;announced government-funded projects to support the build-out of our first utility-scale quantum computers in Brisbane, Australia, and Chicago, Illinois. These initiatives reflect a growing recognition that quantum computing will be strategically and economically defining—and that now is the time to scale.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">PsiQuantum&nbsp;also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. The optical architecture group are specifically responsible for:</p> <ul> <li>discovering and developing new schemes for photonic quantum computation</li> <li>translating abstract quantum information protocols into the designs of physical systems</li> <li>modelling quantum optical systems to determine the requirements for hardware systems</li> </ul> <p>Internships are hired on a rolling basis, with durations of 3 to 6 months. <li>Simulate and benchmark different protocols.</li> <li>Document and communicate results.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Experience/Qualifications:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Degree in: Physics, Math, Computer title: Forward Deployed Architect
description: Who We Are Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: As a Forward Deployed Architect on Notion’s Services team, you will help customers turn AI ambition into operational reality and unlock the full potential of our platform. You will partner directly with customers to design, build, and launch AI-native workflows that drive adoption, usage, and measurable business outcomes. This role sits at the center of Notion’s workflow-led GTM motion. You will partner directly with customers to understand their business goals, operating processes, technical environment, governance needs, and adoption barriers, then translate that context into scalable Notion architectures that drive measurable value. You will be hands-on across discovery, solution design, workspace architecture, workflow build, AI implementation, launch planning, adoption and handoff. You will work deeply with customers to define what Notion should own, where it should integrate with existing systems, and how Notion can become a durable operating layer for their teams. The best candidates combine strong consultative discovery, systems thinking, technical fluency, AI-native workflow design, implementation judgment and exceptional customer presence. You should be comfortable reasoning through technical tradeoffs, designing scalable solutions, and partnering closely with Forward Deployed Engineering when deeper engineering support is required. What You'll Achieve: Partner with customers on forward deployed engagements from discovery through launch, translating business goals and workflow requirements into scalable clear solution design and Notion solutions that drive durable adoption. Design scalable Notion architectures that translate customer workflows, permission and governance needs, integrations and AI use cases into optimal workspaces that are easy to adopt, manage and scale. Design and deploy AI-native workflows using Notion AI, custom agents, automations, Workers, Developer Platform capabilities and adjacent AI tools, partnering with Forward Deployed Engineering when advanced technical depth is needed for migrations, API constraints, security architecture or frontier implementation. Help customers navigate change by designing adoption plans, enablement materials and launch approaches that drive sustained usage and measurable business value. Identify repeatable patterns across customer engagements and convert them into packaged solutions, templates, reference architectures, run books, enablement assets and product feedback. Serve as a trusted advisor to customers, simplifying complex technical requirements, making practical tradeoff recommendations and helping stakeholders align around a clear implementation path. Partner cross-functionally with GTM, Product, Engineering, PMM, Services leadership and the partner ecosystem to scale what works beyond individual customer engagements. Create clear implementation plans, handoff materials and success measures that align customers and internal teams on the path to value. Skills You'll Need to Bring: 5+ years of experience in tech services/consulting, solutions architecture, implementation, customer engineering, or a similar customer-facing role. Proven ability to translate ambiguous customer goals into clear workflows, implementation plans, solution architectures, and measurable success criteria. Strong consultative discovery skills, including the ability to map current-state workflows, identify customer pain, understand operating models, surface technical constraints, and define practical future-state solutions. Hands-on AI builder mindset, with experience using AI tools to design, prototype, automate, or improve real business workflows. Technical fluency with APIs, integrations, data models, automation, enterprise systems, developer workflows and implementation tradeoffs. You do not need to write production code but you should be able to reason through technical constraints and troubleshoot effectively. Strong experience delivering implementations that drive adoption, change management and long-term customer value. Strong project and engagement management skills, including ownership of scope, timeline, deliverables, stakeholder alignment, risks, decisions, dependencies and launch readiness. Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to simplify complex technical concepts for business, technical, and executive audiences. Strong executive presence and customer judgment, with the ability to build trust, frame tradeoffs clearly, and move ambiguous decisions forward. Bias toward action, high learning velocity, and comfort building in fast-changing AI-native product environments. Nice to Haves: Experience designing or deploying Agents, automations or AI-powered workflows with Customers. Experience with Notion, APIs, MCPs, Workers, coding agents or developer platform workflows. Experience developing discovery methodologies, reusable delivery assets, internal tooling, packaged services or reference architectures from the ground up. Experience partnering with Product and Engineering teams to turn field learnings into roadmap signal, reusable architecture patterns or scalable product improvements. Previous experience in a fast-paced, high-growth technology environment. By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy . #LI-Onsite A Note on AI You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. Equal Opportunity & Accommodations We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Notion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Consistent with applicable law, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Notion provides reasonable accommodations during the application process; if you need one, please let your recruiter know. Notion is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Notion considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Notion is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let your recruiter know. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: <p><em data-stringify-type="italic">We are open to hiring at multiple levels for this role, depending on experience, impact, and demonstrated ownership. While this role is level-agnostic, it is best suited for engineers with experience owning production systems and working in highly ambiguous problem spaces.</em></p> <p><strong>Software Engineer</strong></p> <p><strong>About the company:&nbsp;</strong></p> <p>In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.</p> <p>KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.</p> <p>Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health &amp; safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.</p> <p>KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.</p> <p>KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.</p> <p>We are hiring Software Engineers to accelerate our mission.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>About The Role:</strong></p> <p>At KoBold, software engineers have the unique opportunity to embed directly with their users and learn the ins and outs of mineral exploration and geology while developing state of the art technology solutions. Unlike traditional software engineering roles, we don’t simply ship code and passively wait for feedback about its utility: our userbase includes our colleagues… and ourselves! While there are real technical challenges in making mineral exploration data broadly searchable and accessible to both humans and machines, we believe that solving these technical challenges cannot be done without “getting our hands dirty” – sometimes literally! – by embedding directly with the exploration teams and even occasionally (~once a year) joining our colleagues in the field, be it in Zambia, Canada, or Arizona, to experience the impact of our software in real time.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>As a Software Engineer on the Data Systems Engineering team at KoBold, your main role will be to enable systematic exploration and materially improve exploration success rates by making mineral exploration data broadly accessible to humans and machines.&nbsp; Past projects have included SIP (the Structured Ingest Pipeline), DataKit generation (producing curated sets of data on demand), and RAG (Retrieval Augmentation Generation, utilizing natural language processing on unstructured data). Our tech stack is primarily python and includes Django, React, AWS, and additional technologies like Retool and Prefect.&nbsp;</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>Your work will empower KoBold to unlock invaluable insights and streamline intricate scientific processes. Collaborating with our exceptional team of data scientists, geologists, and other software engineers, you will have the opportunity to tackle complex problems head-on and collectively pave the way for the discoveries of vital energy transition metals like lithium, copper, nickel, and cobalt. Together we can shape the future of mineral exploration and contribute to building a sustainable world.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>This role be responsible for:</p> <ul> <li>Deep engagement with exploration geologists and data scientists, continual learning about mineral exploration, and tailoring technology development to the needs of exploration project scientists</li> <li>Building data pipelines and tooling for deriving advanced human and machine insights from exploration data, often leading a small group of software engineers to successful delivery</li> <li>Developing expertise in KoBold’s Data Systems and deeply understanding how they impact exploration</li> <li>End-to-end ownership of projects from design to implementation and testing to continued engagement with colleagues on exploration teams using your solutions</li> <li>Responding well to design and code feedback, also providing feedback to teammates&nbsp;</li> <li>Operationally managing the team’s services and assisting scientific colleagues with our tooling</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>4+ years of software engineering experience, ideally building production cloud data systems</li> <li>Proficiency with Python</li> <li>Ability to write production-quality code that is correct, readable, well-tested, scalable and extensible</li> <li>Skilled in large-scale system design</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership from definition of the problem and delivering projects with demonstrated impact in an iterative manner</li> <li>Intellectual curiosity and eagerness to learn about all aspects of mineral exploration, particularly in the geology domain. Enjoys constantly learning such that you are driving insights through using our tools in exploration and willing to work directly with geologists in the field.</li> <li>Ability to explain technical problems to and collaborate on solutions with domain experts who are not software developers. A strong communicator who enjoys working with colleagues across the company.</li> <li>Excitement about joining a fast-growing early-stage company, comfort with a dynamic work environment, and eagerness to take on an evolving range of responsibilities.</li> <li>Keen not just to build cool technology, but to figure out what technical product to build to best achieve the business objectives of the company.</li> </ul> <p>Nice to Haves&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Experience with modern frontend frameworks such as React</li> <li>Experience with geospatial data and building map-based experiences</li> <li>Familiarity with containerization and container orchestration platforms, such as Docker, AWS ECS, Kubernetes, etc.</li> <li>Formal education or job exposure to natural sciences</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p>The UK base salary range for this full-time exempt position is $120,000 - $210,000 USD.</p> <p>Location: Remote, Candidates can be located anywhere in the United Kingdom.&nbsp;</p> <div class=""><a name="app"></a></div> <p><strong>What to Expect</strong></p> <p>Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p><p>Compensation ranges are listed in USD. If you are based outside the US, the range may not translate directly: US pay reflects a different market with different competitive dynamics, so we benchmark roles against the local market rather than converting the listed figure.</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

Heidi's UK and Europe business is growing faster than the finance scaffolding underneath it. Central finance across Sydney, Melbourne and Manila runs month-end close, core accounting and day-to-day operations, but the region needs someone on the ground who owns the accuracy of its numbers and sits close enough to the commercial team to shape decisions before they get made. Today, regional leaders wait on Australian hours for answers about their own P&L. You'll end that.

The role has two halves and both carry equal weight. You'll own regional financial control and compliance: the integrity of the balance sheet, the accuracy of management reporting and forecasts, cash, strong local controls, and statutory obligations across Companies House, HMRC and VAT, directed through external advisers. You'll also be a hands-on business partner to UK and Europe leadership, Sales and Customer Success, owning the P&L narrative, bringing a commercial view to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, and making sure teams see the financial consequence of the choices they make. You'll report to the Group Financial Controller with a dotted line to FP&A.

What you'll do

Financial reporting and month-end close

  • Own the integrity of the UK&Europe balance sheet, with reconciliations that stay current, reviewed and explainable

  • Own the accuracy of the UK&Europe monthly group reporting and management accounts with variance commentary that explains movements

  • Be the single point of contact for group finance on anything UK&Europe: queries, adjustments, restatements, consolidation-level questions

Compliance and risk oversight

  • Own the UK&Europe compliance calendar (Companies House, HMRC, VAT) by directing external accountants and advisers

  • Own the adviser relationships (accounting, tax, audit), keeping work well scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi's internal finance standards

  • Build an early-warning process so compliance risk is caught and escalated well before it threatens trading status

  • Be the accountable owner if something in the compliance chain breaks down

Commercial business partnering

  • Be the day-to-day finance partner to UK&Europe leadership, owning the regional P&L narrative, budget vs actual and the "why" behind the numbers

  • Bring a commercial lens to pricing, deal terms and customer economics, flagging risk and opportunity early

  • Translate regional performance into clear, decision-ready input for FP&A and company leadership

  • Give UK&Europe business leaders a reliable, self-serve view of their numbers, so decisions stop waiting on Australian hours

  • Feed central finance the regional inputs it needs at close: accrual estimates, revenue and spend context, then review and sign off on the UK&Europe result

Revenue risk and collections

  • Partner with Sales and Customer Success to resolve aged and disputed balances and unblock stuck revenue

  • Own the commercial view of collection risk: which accounts, why, and what it means for cash, and feed it into forecasting

  • Drive down UK&Europe DSO by fixing the upstream causes (contracting, disputes, process), not by chasing invoices

FinOps, controls and performance frameworks

  • Build the operating rhythm that turns UK&Europe finance from reactive support into a reliable performance framework: clear KPIs, owners, review cadences and escalation paths

  • Partner with budget owners on spend decisions before they are made, rather than policing them after the fact

  • Strengthen financial controls across spend, approvals, vendor onboarding, card usage, subscriptions and commercial commitments, while keeping the process pragmatic for a fast-moving region

  • Review regional AP and card activity, including prompt removal of leaver access and cards, and escalate anomalies to central finance operations

  • Partner with external accountants, tax advisers, compliance providers and other vendors, making sure work is well-scoped, reviewed and connected back to Heidi’s internal finance standards

  • Use FinOps-style discipline to connect spend, usage and outcomes, especially across tooling, GTM systems, implementation costs and region-specific operating expenses

  • Create simple documentation and control checks so the region can scale without relying on informal knowledge or one-off fixes

What you'll need

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen — comfortable moving between P&L narrative, deal economics and cash impact

  • Experience business partnering with Sales, Customer Success or regional leadership in a growth business

  • Track record improving collections or DSO by fixing root causes, not just process

  • Experience owning spend or expense controls in a way that supports the business rather than only governing it

  • Comfortable directing (not necessarily performing) statutory compliance and VAT work through external advisers

  • High degree of autonomy and ownership in a small, remote-first global finance team

  • Clear, confident communicator — able to hold your own with commercial leaders and external advisers alike

  • Experience in a multi-entity or multi-currency business

Nice to have

  • Experience in a high-growth SaaS or technology company

  • Qualified accountant (ACA / ACCA / CIMA or equivalent)

  • Exposure to Companies House, HMRC and Irish Revenue processes

  • Experience with Campfire, Airwallex or similar modern finance tooling

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You'll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we'd like to see. We're medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who've felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we're building isn't always easy. But we didn't choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn't whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you're doing the defining work of your career.

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year, Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement. Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply. What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator. What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. Conditions Twelve-month fixed-term contract under French public law, full time (1 607 h annual reference), 25 working days of annual leave plus the RTT days of the establishment’s scheme. Affiliation to the régime général for health and to IRCANTEC for supplementary pension; employer contribution to complementary health cover under the scheme in force at the establishment; 75 % reimbursement of publictransport season tickets, up to the statutory ceiling. The exact number of RTT days is set by the establishment. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

At OPENLANE, we make wholesale easy so our customers can be more successful. We're a technology company, building the world's most advanced - and simple - digital marketplace for used vehicles. We're a data company, helping customers buy and sell smarter with clear, actionable insights they can understand and use. And we're an innovative company accelerating the future of wholesale remarketing through curiosity, collaboration, and an entrepreneurial spirit. OPENLANE offers its customers the best digital marketplace for used cars in Europe. Our B2B clients enjoy operational excellence when working with us.

Our Values

  • Driven Waybuilders: We pursue challenges that inspire us to build, create and innovate.
  • Relentless Curiosity: We seek to understand and improve our customers' experience.
  • Smart Risk-Taking: We transform risk into progress through data, experience, and intuition.
  • Fearless Ownership: We deliver what we promise and learn along the way.


What are we looking for?
Do you have a strong commercial mindset, a sharp analytical eye and a passion for driving business performance?

OPENLANE Europe is looking for an experienced Head of Commercial Excellence who understands what drives commercial success and knows how to translate insights into measurable results.

With operations across more than 20 countries, we're looking for someone who sees the bigger picture, understands the dynamics of different markets and recognizes opportunities to improve. Someone who enjoys working closely with commercial teams, bringing fresh perspectives and helping turn business insights into better decisions.

As our Head of Commercial Excellence, you'll have the opportunity to build and shape this function from the ground up. Working alongside country managers and senior leadership, you'll play an important role in strengthening commercial decision-making and driving performance across our European organization.

What will you do?

  • Build and lead our Commercial Excellence function, developing a team across sales operations and commercial analytics.
  • Establish consistent commercial KPIs, reporting standards and performance insights across European markets.
  • Translate commercial data into actionable recommendations to improve conversion rates, commission per vehicle and overall business performance.
  • Drive commercial performance reviews, providing meaningful insights to support better business decisions.
  • Develop commercial scorecards and variable compensation frameworks, aligning performance measures with business objectives.
  • Evaluate pricing strategies and promotional initiatives to identify opportunities for improved commercial returns.
  • Lead data-driven commercial planning and forecasting, considering market dynamics, volumes and seasonality.
  • Partner with country managers and senior leadership to identify opportunities, challenge assumptions constructively and drive measurable commercial improvements.

Requirements

Who are you?

  • You bring solid experience in commercial excellence, commercial performance, sales operations or analytics, ideally within an international organization.
  • You are fluent in English, both written and spoken. Knowledge of another European language is an advantage.
  • You combine a strong commercial mindset with excellent analytical skills, and enjoy working hands-on with data to identify opportunities and drive business improvements.

  • You communicate confidently, build strong relationships and know how to influence senior stakeholders through clear, fact-based recommendations.

title: Founding Data Researcher
description: TL;DR Davis is hiring a Founding Data Researcher to build the data behind our foundation model, trained from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. You will own the data end to end, from raw floorplans and synthetic generation to a canonical representation, curation, large-scale pretraining and the ablations that tell us which data actually moves the model. Here the dataset is part of the algorithm. About Davis Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate four to five fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they will need only one: Davis. We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability. We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital , with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end. The Role You will own the data our foundation model learns from, a model we train from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically. You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture. You are senior enough to architect the data stack and set the data strategy, and hands-on enough to write the pipelines, run the experiments, train the models and do the ablations yourself. What you will be working on Corpus from raw sources. Turn real floorplans (images, PDFs, scans) into clean, standardized building graphs, with the geometry and semantics that make them trainable. Synthetic data generation. Explore strategies to expand the dataset with synthetic data. Canonical representation and curation. Define the standardized representation, then filter, deduplicate, quality-score and validate at scale, with versioning, provenance and lineage. Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining. Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture. Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time. What We Are Looking For You have built the dataset, not just trained on it. You have personally built or generated the data used for a large pretraining run, from raw or synthetic sources, rather than only training on a dataset someone handed you. Senior and deeply hands-on. At least 5 years of strong experience, senior enough to architect the data stack and set strategy, but still coding the pipelines, running the experiments and doing the ablations yourself. Data as a first-class problem. A track record where the data itself is the object: curation, filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixtures, synthetic generation. Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture. Nice to have Computer vision and document understanding , images to structured output, OCR, layout extraction, segmentation, geometry extraction, vectorization, raster to vector, image to scene graph, 3D or CAD. Graph and structured scientific data , molecular, protein or scene graphs, meshes, CAD, BIM, 3D geometry, or relational and structured world data. Synthetic worlds and simulation , a structured state to a simulator to a renderer to synthetic images with perfect labels, then a perception model, with an eye on the sim-to-real gap. Foundation models from scratch , real involvement in a large pretraining run, not only fine-tuning. Public evidence of data ownership , lead on a dataset, a Hugging Face release, a dataset card, a technical blog on your pipeline, or a talk on data curation or synthetic data. GIS and geometry , parcels, zoning layers, projections, computational geometry or constrained optimization. Multi-country data , heterogeneous sources, localization and varying rules. Why Join Davis Own the data end to end , from the generator to the pretraining mixture, as the person who defines what the model learns from. The Role

Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically.

You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture.   • Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining.

  • Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture.

  • Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time.

  • Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture.

raw.title: AI Engineer
raw.description:
Alassio recherche son (sa) prochain(e) AI Engineer !

 
 

Missions

 

🏗️ Alassio en quelques mots

En France, la paie et le social comptent parmi les fonctions les plus réglementées qui soient. Entre inflation réglementaire et évolutions légales et conventionnelles incessantes, la conformité est devenue un véritable fardeau pour les cabinets de paie et les services RH :

  • ce fardeau les empêche de se consacrer à ce qui compte vraiment, le conseil et l'accompagnement des salariés, qui en subissent donc eux aussi le poids

  • c'est aussi l'un des métiers où l'attrition est la plus forte en France, notamment parce que 60 % du temps des gestionnaires de paie est encore consacré à de la saisie ou à de la relecture manuelle

Pourtant, des solutions technologiques majeures existent : l'IA permet en particulier d'automatiser une très grande partie des tâches les plus pénibles et de valoriser les données sociales. Mais le secteur reste largement à l'écart de cette révolution, et le problème n'est pas seulement réglementaire : le marché était verrouillé par des éditeurs historiques vieillissants, difficiles à quitter faute d'alternative crédible et de moyens pour migrer efficacement. Là aussi, l'IA fait voler ces barrières en éclats et ouvre la voie à une vague d'innovation attendue depuis des décennies.

C'est pour y répondre qu'Alassio construit la plateforme de paie et de gestion RH moderne qui manquait à ce marché, au service des cabinets et de leurs clients TPE/PME. Notre ambition est de développer en un temps record :

  • une plateforme collaborative et ouverte, qui s'intègre nativement aux outils des cabinets et de leurs clients, respecte leurs habitudes de travail et fluidifie les échanges entre gestionnaires de paie et entreprises

  • l'automatisation de la tenue administrative : collecte des données, paramétrage des évolutions légales et des règles propres à chaque entreprise, génération automatique des rapports et formulaires, traçabilité juridique dynamique et en temps réel, etc.

  • la valorisation des données de paie et sociales, pour offrir un conseil social à 360° et enfin répondre efficacement à l'ensemble des attentes des salariés, qui se sont de surcroît largement amplifiées depuis le Covid : gestion contractuelle, pilotage de la masse salariale, avantages salariés, fidélisation des talents, mutuelle…

L'objectif : devenir le « People OS » sur lequel les cabinets et leurs clients TPE/PME s'appuient pour gérer l'intégralité de leurs problématiques paie et RH.

 

🚀 Tes responsabilités

Ta mission : faire de l'IA le levier qui démultiplie le travail de chacun chez Alassio. L'objectif est assumé : multiplier par 10 la productivité de chaque membre de l'équipe.

  • Tu formes la Growth squad avec notre Founding Strategy & Operations : ce binôme transverse optimise l'existant, automatise les workflows de toutes les équipes et fait passer nos initiatives IA et nos outils internes à l'échelle : hébergement et mise en production dans des environnements partagés, sécurité, observabilité, optimisation et amélioration continue

  • Tu deviens le (la) référent(e) IA d'Alassio : on se veut profondément AI-native et on expérimente énormément. Tu centralises et coordonnes ces initiatives pour que ce "lab interne" soit efficace, et tu expérimentes aussi en continu avec toutes les techno IA (budget et outillage conséquents)

  • Tu construis la nouvelle colonne vertébrale IT d'Alassio, en identifiant les systèmes IA qui comptent à l'échelle de toute l'entreprise

  • Tu prépares l'avenir du produit : à terme, les usages testés et éprouvés en interne sous ton impulsion ont vocation à rejoindre notre plateforme. Ils nourriront le « People OS » qui démocratise les cas d'usage les plus pertinents de l'IA dans notre secteur

 

🧭 Tes premiers chantiers

Ton point de départ : Bedrock, notre OS interne. Un peu à la manière de Palantir Foundry, il agrège & orchestre tout le contexte de l'entreprise pour en tirer des actions concrètes : suivi ultra-personnalisé et automatisé de nos utilisateurs, analyse produit, documentation, rédaction de tickets et PR associées…

Bedrock est déjà au cœur du quotidien de toutes les équipes. Mais il s'est construit par couches successives, au fil des cas d'usage ajoutés. Ton premier objectif est d'en dresser l'inventaire complet, process et outils IA compris. Tu définis ensuite la roadmap qui le fera changer de dimension :

  • Workflows : optimiser l'existant

  • Infrastructure : sécurité, confidentialité, hébergement et environnements partagés, pour un OS multi-joueur, plug-and-play et scalable

  • Observabilité : suivre les agents et leur performance, et améliorer chaque logique en continu

  • Autonomie : construire des workflows agentiques déclenchés par webhook ou planifiés, qui nettoient le contexte et mènent des missions 24/7

Très vite, tu as vocation à devenir le (la) responsable qui orchestre l'IA chez Alassio, et le (la) référent(e) de notre OS Bedrock.

 
 

Profil recherché

 

🌱 Expérience

  • 1 à 2 ans d'expérience dans un rôle d'AI Engineer / FDE / AI Deployment Strategist dans une top structure tech (BCGX, Palantir, Dust)

  • Plusieurs missions concrètes de déploiement et d'optimisation de technologies IA : mise en place de zéro d'un workflow au sein d'une organisation, sujets de gouvernance et de déploiement en entreprise, etc.

  • Une utilisation intensive des outils IA et une bonne maîtrise de Python : Claude Code / Codex ; Cursor Agents, Linear/PostHog, déploiement et hébergement (cloud, AI routers, etc.)

 

💎 Qualités

  • Un goût pour l'optimisation et l'organisation : tu aimes que les choses soient claires, que l'information soit facile à mobiliser, propre et maintenable, et tu prends plaisir à produire vite des éléments actionnables

  • Un biais très fort pour l'action : tu repères les problèmes avant qu'on te les signale, et tu ne t'arrêtes jamais au diagnostic

  • Penser à l'échelle : tu conçois dès le départ des solutions capables d'encaisser des montées en charge ×10 ou ×100, tout en restant pragmatique sur ce qui compte à court et moyen terme

 
 

Processus de sélection

  1. Premier entretien avec Tancrède (CEO) : 45 min

  2. Étude de cas technique avec Hector (COO) et Ivan Robert (Founding SWE) : 1h30

  3. Rencontre informelle de l'équipe dans nos bureaux, puis échange de 45 min avec les fondateurs Ayoub (CAIO), Paul (CTO), Tancrède (CEO) & Hector (COO)

  4. Deux à trois prises de référence

 
 

Ce que nous offrons

 

👊 Une mission unique

Tu rejoins une aventure entrepreneuriale en plein passage à l'échelle, sur un marché verrouillé depuis des années. On est convaincus que l'IA ne transformera pas seulement le produit et secteur qu'on construit, mais aussi la façon avec laquelle toutes les entreprises devront se réinventer. On en fait déjà l'expérience au quotidien avec Bedrock, notre OS interne qui est aujourd'hui au cœur de l'activité de toutes nos équipes tech et non-tech.

Ton rôle est de faire passer ce laboratoire à l'échelle pour que chaque équipe d'Alassio aille plus vite, avec l'ambition assumée de bâtir une référence en matière d'organisation AI-native.

 

🎁 Rémunération et avantages

  • 💰 Package de 70 à 90K€ + BSPCE

  • 🏥 Mutuelle Alan

  • 🍽️ Carte Swile (titres-restaurant)

  • 💻 Top matériel IT (MacOS, écran incurvé)

  • 🤓 Offsite légendaires

 

➡️ Prochaines étapes

C'est un poste à la fois de pilotage et de terrain : en lien avec les équipes Sales et Product, tu mènes le projet de migration du cabinet, tu assures la formation initiale de ses gestionnaires de paie et tu animes les points de suivi tout au long de la phase pilote et des premiers mois de production.

 

🧩 Les étapes d'un déploiement

  1. Cadrage : kick-off structuré avec le cabinet, ateliers de recueil des besoins (conventions, spécificités des dossiers, reprise d'historique), planning partagé

  2. Pilote : formation initiale des gestionnaires de paie, migration d'un premier échantillon de dossiers, paies en parallèle et contrôle des écarts

  3. Déploiement : bascule progressive de dossiers supplémentaires selon le planning défini en amont, mise en production

  4. Suivi actif : accompagnement renforcé après le démarrage, puis passage de relais à l'équipe Support

 

🧭 Tes missions

  • Piloter le déploiement d'un portefeuille de 5 à 10 cabinets selon leur taille

  • Être l'interlocuteur de référence du responsable social du cabinet et de ses gestionnaires de paie ; animer les points d'étape et un bilan régulier avec chaque cabinet

  • Former les équipes : formation initiale des gestionnaires de paie, sessions de prise en main, approfondissements

  • Suivre la migration : reprise des données et des historiques, paramétrage des dossiers avec l'Ingénieur(e) Paramétrage Paie, paies en parallèle et contrôle des écarts

  • Coordonner les équipes internes mobilisées sur le cabinet : Sales, paramétrage, support, produit

  • Construire et faire évoluer le playbook de migration : étapes, checklists, supports de formation, indicateurs de suivi

  • Faire remonter au Product les besoins et les irritants observés sur le terrain

 

📊 Indicateurs de réussite

  • Satisfaction des cabinets de ton portefeuille

  • Respect du planning de déploiement

  • Rapidité de résolution des demandes, en lien avec les autres équipes d'Alassio

  • Adoption d'Alassio par les gestionnaires de paie du cabinet

 

🤝 Ton environnement

  • Rattachement : Alexandre (Responsable Déploiement & Accompagnement), au sein de l'équipe DnA

  • Tu travailles en lien étroit avec l'équipe Sales et l'équipe Métier

  • Outils : Alassio, Notion, Qualiobee

 

🗓️ Tes 6 premiers mois

  • À 1 mois : tu maîtrises l'outil et le playbook de migration, et tu co-pilotes un premier déploiement en binôme

  • À 3 mois : tu pilotes en autonomie tes premiers cabinets et tu contribues à l'amélioration du processus d'onboarding des cabinets

  • À 6 mois : tu gères un portefeuille complet de 5 à 10 cabinets, dont tu mènes entièrement le déploiement sur Alassio

Indispensable :

  • Formation en paie (BTS, licence pro, master ou titre professionnel Gestionnaire de paie) ou Bac+3 en RH

  • Au moins 3 ans d'expérience en paie, en cabinet d'expertise comptable ou chez un éditeur

  • Pratique d'un logiciel de paie du marché

  • Une expérience de migration de logiciel de paie ou de projet de déploiement

  • De l'aisance dans l'animation de formations

  • Sens de l'organisation et de la gestion de projet ; excellent relationnel, y compris avec des décisionnaires

  • Mobilité pour des déplacements ponctuels chez nos cabinets partenaires

Un plus :

  • Expérience de consultant(e) chez un éditeur de paie

  • Bonne connaissance de la DSN et des environnements multi-conventions

  • Expérience de conception de supports de formation

 

💎 Qualités

  • Une posture de conseil, adaptable au contexte de chaque cabinet

  • La pédagogie, la rigueur et le sens du suivi

  • Le calme et la fiabilité dans les moments sensibles d'une mise en production et lors des pics d'activité (clôtures de paie, mois de janvier)

raw.title: Backend Engineer - Platform Core
raw.description:
Backend Engineer (Golang) – Platform Core

Location: Remote, European time zones, Full-time, Permanent

About FullEnrich:

Every go-to-market motion runs on data, but no single provider has ever had complete coverage. We solve that problem with waterfall enrichment: instead of relying on a single data source, we orchestrate 20+ premium providers around the world, automatically querying them until we find the best available contact information. The result is industry-leading coverage and data quality, helping sales and GTM teams connect with the right people faster.

What started as a better way to find emails and phone numbers has grown into a broader vision: becoming the trusted B2B data layer powering modern revenue teams and AI-driven workflows alike. Today, more than 5,000 customers, including companies like AWS, Deel, HubSpot, Clay, and Artisan, trust us to power their prospecting and enrichment.

Founded in Paris and now headquartered in San Francisco, we're a team of 50+ people across the US, Europe, LATAM, and Israel, growing quickly and building with speed, ownership, and ambition. That's where you come in.

About the Role:

At the heart of FullEnrich is our waterfall engine. It's the system responsible for deciding which data providers to call, in what order, under which conditions, and what happens when something fails. It works well today, but what we're building next is significantly more ambitious.

We're evolving the engine to become far more flexible and configurable, supporting account-specific requirements, dynamic routing based on different optimization goals, and seamless integration of new providers and behaviors without introducing unnecessary complexity.

This is a foundational part of our product, and getting the architecture right is critical to how we scale.

We're looking for an experienced Backend Engineer who enjoys solving complex infrastructure challenges and taking ownership of the systems behind them.

If you've built high-throughput routing systems, designed multi-provider orchestration layers, or worked on infrastructure that needs to adapt to different customers and use cases, this is exactly the kind of challenge you'll be taking on.

What You'll Do:

  • Own and evolve our core routing engine: Take ownership of provider selection, fallback logic, load balancing, and queue management. Our waterfall currently operates as a modular Go monolith, and you'll help evolve it to support account-level customization at scale without introducing unnecessary complexity.

  • Build and improve provider integrations: Design how we connect to and manage third-party data providers, focusing on rate limiting, reliability, and observability. This includes supporting external provider credentials, configurable provider ordering, and well-defined fallback behavior when providers are unavailable.

  • Develop intelligent routing capabilities: Build the logic that dynamically selects providers based on different optimization objectives, including speed, coverage, compliance, and intelligent load balancing, while managing rate limits effectively.

  • Design scalable multi-tenant architecture: Develop the foundations for sub-accounts, customer-specific credit pools, and endpoint-level configuration, ensuring the engine remains flexible, scalable, and maintainable.

  • Build composable verification workflows: Integrate validity and compliance checks into the enrichment pipeline as configurable steps, allowing results to be independently verified regardless of their original data source.

  • Strengthen our core architecture: Improve and refactor existing systems as we scale, applying strong engineering practices to keep our codebase clean, understandable, reliable, and easy to maintain.

  • Shape technical decisions: Work closely with our engineering leadership to translate product requirements into thoughtful architectural solutions, balancing immediate needs with long-term scalability.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 3 months:

  • Develop a deep understanding of our existing waterfall engine, provider integrations, and core backend architecture.

  • Build strong relationships with the engineering team and identify opportunities to improve reliability, performance, and maintainability.

  • Start contributing to the evolution of our routing engine, taking ownership of initial architectural improvements and technical decisions.

By 6 months:

  • Take ownership of key components of our core platform, delivering meaningful improvements to provider orchestration, fallback logic, and routing capabilities.

  • Help introduce more flexible, account-level configuration while keeping the architecture clean, scalable, and maintainable.

  • Improve the reliability and observability of our provider integrations, reducing operational complexity as we scale.

By 12 months:

  • Play a leading role in delivering a more intelligent, configurable waterfall engine that supports different customer needs and optimization goals at scale.

  • Establish robust architectural foundations for multi-tenancy, composable verification, and continued provider expansion.

  • Be a trusted technical contributor within the engineering team, helping shape long-term architectural decisions and ensuring our core platform remains reliable, performant, and ready for future growth.

What We're Looking For:

  • Strong backend engineering experience: You've built and maintained production systems involving routing, fallback mechanisms, queues, concurrency, and rate limiting. You understand how distributed and multi-provider systems behave under pressure and how to design for reliability.

  • An architecture-first mindset: You're comfortable taking a product requirement, identifying potential structural challenges, and designing solutions that will stand the test of time. You think beyond implementation and consider scalability, maintainability, and long-term impact.

  • Deep experience with Golang: Go is at the core of our backend. You're confident working with modular architectures, clean code principles, and ideally hexagonal architecture.

  • Experience managing technical complexity: You can navigate systems with multiple interconnected components, from account-level configuration and provider orchestration to compliance workflows and multi-tenancy, without compromising clarity or simplicity.

  • Strong ownership and problem-solving skills: You're proactive, pragmatic, and comfortable making technical decisions. You enjoy getting into the details, understanding why systems behave the way they do, and finding solutions to challenging engineering problems.

  • A collaborative approach: You communicate clearly, challenge ideas constructively, and enjoy working with other engineers to build reliable, high-quality systems.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with data routing, enrichment pipelines, or multi-provider orchestration systems.

  • Experience building API marketplace infrastructure or multi-tenant SaaS backends.

  • Familiarity with API-first product architectures.

  • An interest in the evolving data infrastructure landscape.

Our Tech Stack

Our backend is built primarily in Golang, following a modular, hexagonal architecture.

Our wider stack includes:

  • Backend: Go (Golang)

  • Databases & Search: PostgreSQL, OpenSearch

  • Infrastructure: DigitalOcean, Docker

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions

  • Monitoring & Observability: Grafana

You'll be joining an engineering team of around 10 people, working on one of the most critical components of our platform.

Interview Process

We aim to keep our process straightforward, transparent, and focused on getting to know each other.

  1. Introduction to FullEnrich with our Talent team (30 min) – A chance to learn more about you, introduce FullEnrich and the role, and explore whether there's a mutual fit.

  2. CTO & VP Engineering Interview (60 minutes): A conversation about your experience, the role, and a technical discussion based on a real experiment.

  3. Technical Assessment: A take-home exercise completed in your own time, followed by a review and discussion.

  4. Team & Culture Interview: Meet with a member of the team to learn more about how we work together and ensure there's a strong mutual fit.

title: Junior Network & IT Security Engineer (a)
description: Dein künftiger Arbeitgeber ist ein internationales tätiges Schweizer Familienunternehmen der Industrietechnologie mit Sitz in der Ostschweiz. Seine Produkte stecken in Maschinen und Anlagen auf der ganzen Welt, entsprechend vernetzt ist die IT-Landschaft mit Standorten auf mehreren Kontinenten. Das IT-Security-Team schützt diese globale Infrastruktur und baut die Sicherheit Schritt für Schritt weiter aus. Für den Einstieg in dieses Team suchen wir eine Person, die technisch solide startet und Security mit Begeisterung in die Organisation trägt. Meine Herausforderungen Sicherheitsmassnahmen für Netzwerk und IT-Infrastruktur an allen Standorten umsetzen und laufend weiterentwickeln. Sicherheitsvorfälle und Bedrohungen analysieren, passende Massnahmen einleiten und die Ursachen nachhaltig beheben. Sicherheitsüberprüfungen, Schwachstellenanalysen und Audits durchführen und die Verbesserungen bis zur Umsetzung begleiten. Sicherheitsrichtlinien, Standards und Prozesse mitgestalten und so verankern, dass sie im Alltag gelebt werden. Mit Fachbereichen und IT-Teams zusammenarbeiten, damit Sicherheitsanforderungen schon in frühen Projektphasen einfliessen.
